# Kansas — Builder Mode

Builder-mode derivation constraint: builder-mode content derives strictly from normalized jurisdiction layers.

## corridor_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as a corridor-structured environment where inland transport and logistics visibility is organized around documented turnpike and multimodal freight systems rather than a uniformly described statewide mesh.

## municipal_structure_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as a node-concentrated municipal environment with clearer structure in Wichita, Kansas-side Kansas City corridor nodes, and Topeka-centered/statewide governance visibility, with less complete structure outside those areas.

## governance_visibility_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as having visible statewide governance structure for transport and utility domains through documented policy coordination, rail-program administration, utility oversight, and turnpike operations.

## logistics_structure_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as an inland logistics and freight environment with documented rail, intermodal, highway, and freight-policy coordination structures, while preserving that full statewide freight-node hierarchy detail is incomplete.

## research_environment_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as a multi-node research environment anchored in KU, K-State, K-State Olathe, and Wichita State/NIAR systems.

## energy_environment_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as an energy and transmission environment with visible utility-governance and transmission-process structure, while statewide resilience and full generation-delivery transparency remain incompletely documented.

## digital_infrastructure_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as a selective digital-infrastructure environment with documented facility, backbone, and broadband-program visibility at specific nodes and programs, without a complete statewide interconnection and private-facility inventory.

## agricultural_and_industrial_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted as an agricultural-industrial and manufacturing environment with documented continuity across agricultural production systems, manufacturing subsectors, and corridor-linked logistics integration.

## cross_state_adjacency_interpretation

Kansas should be interpreted with limited cross-state adjacency visibility in the current record, where directly documented references are concentrated on Oklahoma-border corridor continuity and Oklahoma City-to-Newton passenger-rail evaluation context.

## Structural exclusions

The current Kansas record does not support builder-mode interpretation as:

- an Atlas surface assignment
- a routing-role assignment
- a coordination-tier assignment
- a statewide hyperscale leadership environment
- a national freight-hub environment
- a national routing-spine environment
- a federal hosting-corridor environment

Builder-mode completeness status: preliminary
Surface assignment status: none

evidence.content:
# Kansas — Evidence Layer

## Wichita aviation and manufacturing concentration

Kansas has documented aviation and manufacturing concentration in the Wichita corridor.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- Kansas Department of Commerce aerospace materials describing Wichita as a concentration point for aerospace and defense research, development, and manufacturing activity
- Wichita State University National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR) materials describing applied aerospace and manufacturing R&D, certification, testing, training, sustainment, and advanced-manufacturing capabilities
- NIAR location materials documenting multiple Wichita-area sites, including ATLAS, HAMR, and other aerospace-testing and manufacturing-support facilities
- Kansas Department of Commerce manufacturing materials describing statewide manufacturing activity that includes aviation-related subsectors

These materials document Wichita-centered aerospace and manufacturing infrastructure without establishing uniform statewide aviation concentration.

## Kansas City (Kansas-side) infrastructure visibility

Kansas has documented infrastructure visibility on the Kansas side of the Kansas City corridor.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- Kansas Department of Commerce logistics materials describing Logistics Park Kansas City in Edgerton, Kansas as a large inland distribution and intermodal environment
- logistics materials describing Kansas-side corridor references where I-35 and I-70 converge in the Kansas City area
- K-State Olathe materials describing research and partnership activity in the greater Kansas City area on the Kansas side
- DataBank materials describing digital-infrastructure facilities in Lenexa, Kansas

These materials document Kansas-side Kansas City corridor infrastructure without attributing Missouri-side assets to Kansas.

## Topeka governance visibility

Kansas has documented statewide governance and regulatory visibility with Topeka-centered state institutions.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- Kansas Department of Transportation (KDOT) freight and rail materials documenting a state unit that develops and coordinates multimodal freight and rail policy
- Kansas Corporation Commission (KCC) electric and transmission-distribution materials documenting utility-rate and utility-oversight functions
- Kansas Turnpike Authority materials documenting a user-fee roadway system and statewide tolling operations

These materials document state governance visibility and transportation and utility oversight functions relevant to infrastructure coordination.

## Inland freight, rail, highway, and logistics visibility

Kansas has documented inland freight, rail, highway, and logistics structure.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- KDOT freight and rail materials documenting state freight and rail policy coordination, rail-improvement programming, and updates to statewide multimodal freight and rail plans
- Kansas Department of Commerce logistics materials describing Class I and short-line rail participation, multimodal logistics framing, and intermodal logistics assets in Kansas
- Kansas Turnpike Authority materials describing a 236-mile roadway from the Oklahoma border to Kansas City
- KDOT passenger-rail materials documenting evaluation of extension from Oklahoma City to Newton, Kansas for connection to Amtrak service

## Energy, power, grid, and transmission environment

Kansas has documented energy and utility-governance visibility.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- KCC electric and transmission-distribution materials documenting oversight and regulatory functions for electric utilities
- KCC transmission references describing statutory treatment for larger transmission-line siting categories in Kansas
- Evergy company-facts and transmission-project materials documenting utility service footprint, transmission and distribution mileage, substation visibility, and active transmission-project workflow

## Research-university continuity

Kansas has documented research-university continuity through major public-university systems.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- University of Kansas Office of Research materials documenting research support systems, centers and labs, and continuing research expenditures
- Kansas State University research materials documenting research-development structures, sponsored-program support, and research-center continuity
- K-State Olathe materials documenting research and industry partnership activity in the Kansas City-side environment
- Wichita State / NIAR materials documenting sustained aerospace and advanced-manufacturing research institutions

## Data-center and digital-infrastructure visibility

Kansas has documented but uneven digital-infrastructure visibility.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- DataBank materials documenting a Lenexa, Kansas data-center campus with colocation and connectivity features
- KanREN materials documenting a statewide research-and-education network backbone with public-university and Kansas City-area points of presence
- KanREN materials documenting 100G and 400G backbone connectivity and linkage to research-network platforms
- IdeaTek and Kansas state broadband-project materials documenting middle-mile and rural-serving broadband expansion initiatives

## Agricultural-industrial or manufacturing continuity

Kansas has documented agricultural-industrial and advanced-manufacturing continuity.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- Kansas Department of Commerce agriculture materials describing broad agricultural production and agriculture-related industrial activity
- Kansas Department of Commerce manufacturing materials documenting large manufacturing employment and firm presence across multiple subsectors
- logistics and manufacturing materials connecting agricultural, food-processing, and industrial operations to multimodal freight and corridor infrastructure

## Municipal asymmetry and incomplete statewide coverage

Kansas has documented node concentration with incomplete statewide documentary coverage.

The current Kansas package preserves evidence of:

- strong concentration of documentary visibility in Wichita, Kansas-side Kansas City corridor nodes, and statewide governance bodies
- thinner direct documentary coverage for municipal variation outside those nodes
- digital and utility evidence that is stronger at specific nodes and programs than as a full statewide inventory

## Limited central-U.S. and cross-state adjacency evidence

The current source set does not provide enough normalized documentary coverage to characterize:

- Missouri adjacency effects as infrastructure consequences beyond Kansas-side corridor references
- Nebraska, Colorado, or Texas adjacency effects as normalized infrastructure consequences
- national routing position or national freight significance as a classification

## Evidence gaps

- complete statewide IX and backbone mapping beyond currently visible KanREN and selected operator materials
- statewide digital-corridor redundancy coverage across Kansas
- broader private colocation and large-facility inventory beyond currently visible Kansas-side facilities
- fuller municipal comparison outside Wichita, Topeka-governance visibility, and Kansas-side Kansas City corridor nodes
- fuller rail-node hierarchy and freight-node inventory coverage statewide
- complete transmission-resilience and generation-delivery transparency statewide
- broader normalized cross-state adjacency evidence with Missouri, Nebraska, Colorado, and Texas
- direct statewide digital-asset statutory posture detail

## Structural exclusions

The current source set does not support statewide routing classification, cross-state spillover characterization, or surface assignment.

Evidence completeness status: preliminary
Surface assignment status: none
